title: Jensen bound for Hedge's averaged predictions
statement:
Fix a learning rate $\eta \in \bbr$, a loss function $\ell : \bbr \to \Omega \to \bbr$, expert predictions $p : \mathrm{Fin}\,T \to \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \bbr$ (with $N \ge 1$), and a sequence of outcomes $o : \mathrm{Fin}\,T \to \Omega$. Suppose $S \subseteq \bbr$ is convex, every expert prediction $p_t(i)$ lies in $S$, and for each round $t$ the map $x \mapsto \ell(x, o_t)$ is convex on $S$. Then the cumulative loss of Hedge's weighted-average predictions is at most the cumulative Hedge loss computed on the induced loss sequence:
\[
  \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \ell\!\left(\widehat{x}_t,\, o_t\right)
  \;\le\;
  \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \sum_{i=1}^{N} p_t(i)\,\ell\!\left(p_t(i), o_t\right),
\]
where $\widehat{x}_t = \sum_{i} p_t(i)\, p_t(i)$ is the Hedge weighted-average prediction at round $t$ and $p_t$ is the Hedge distribution at that round.
hypotheses_covered: S is a convex subset of the reals
every expert prediction lies in S
for each round t, the loss as a function of the prediction is convex on S
replaced:
Summing the per-round Jensen bound over all $T$ rounds, we obtain
\[
  \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T
  \;\le\;
  \texttt{hedgeCumLoss}\,\eta\,L,
\]
i.e.\ the actual cumulative loss of Hedge's convex-combination predictions is at most
the abstract cumulative Hedge loss on the induced expert loss table.
